filename: The ASTE-BGC Data-Assimilative Regional Ocean Biogeochemistry Model.pdf
title: The ASTE-BGC Data-Assimilative Regional Ocean Biogeochemistry Model
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: Provides a 16-year data-assimilated physical-biogeochemical regional state estimate of the North Atlantic Ocean with high resolution (1/3°) and calibrated ecological parameters, suitable for training or benchmarking ML parameterizations of biological carbon pump dynamics, dissolved oxygen, and surface pCO2.
pain_points: Spin-up caused model drift away from the observed state (model attractor vs. data attractor), making initial condition adjustments dominant over parameter tuning.
The Green's Functions method assumes linearity of perturbations, which is challenging for highly nonlinear ocean biogeochemical and ecological processes.
Computational cost of the Green's Functions approach scales linearly with the number of parameter sensitivity experiments.
Sparse observational coverage in space and time, especially in high-latitude/subpolar regions and winter months.
extraction_notes: The primary calibration method is a classical discrete inverse theory / Green's Functions sensitivity optimization rather than deep learning. Machine learning (XGBoost) appears only within third-party evaluation datasets (GOBAI-O2, LDEO-HPD, pCO2-Residual). The project was supported by the LEAP STC.
